paper_title: Benchmarking large language models for automated labeling: The case of issue report classification
task: Automatic issue report labeling in low-resource settings
agent_or_llm_setup: 22 decoder-only LLMs plus BERT-like encoder baselines
baseline_compared: BERT-like encoder models and generative LLMs
key_findings: Benchmarks open/proprietary generative LLMs against encoder models and emphasizes the tradeoff between manual labels and zero-shot inference cost.
relevance_to_autoempirical: Direct baseline for AutoEmpirical filtering because it studies GitHub issue labeling with LLMs and BERT-style models.
notes: Use for LLM-vs-encoder baseline framing.

paper_title: Issue classification with LLMs: An empirical study of the NASA flight software systems
venue_or_source: Journal of Systems and Software / NASA NTRS
task: Bug-ticket identification for flight software issue reports
data_source: NASA cFS and F Prime issue datasets
agent_or_llm_setup: Generative LLMs, GPT-4o, BERT-like encoder models, SetFit
key_findings: Finds small curated training sets with SetFit can outperform zero-shot LLMs in practical issue classification settings.
relevance_to_autoempirical: Relevant because AutoEmpirical also filters defect-related reports and must compare zero-shot prompting with trained lightweight classifiers.
notes: Strong source for cost/labeling tradeoffs.

paper_title: Exploring Fine-Grained Bug Report Categorization with Large Language Models and Prompt Engineering: An Empirical Study
venue_or_source: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
task: Fine-grained bug report categorization
data_source: 1,024 bug reports and 221,184 generated category labels
agent_or_llm_setup: Selected LLMs with multiple prompt engineering strategies
key_findings: Shows prompt design strongly affects consistency and that LLM disagreements can reveal unclear or possibly mislabeled bug reports.
relevance_to_autoempirical: Directly relevant to AutoEmpirical symptom/root-cause taxonomy classification and label-quality auditing.
notes: Use in fine-grained taxonomy discussion.

paper_title: Applying large language models to issue classification: Revisiting with extended data and new models
task: GitHub issue classification with recent LLMs
agent_or_llm_setup: GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o, DeepSeek R1
key_findings: Reports that data quality can matter more than raw dataset size for LLM-based issue classification.
relevance_to_autoempirical: Relevant because Stage-1 unifies labels from heterogeneous empirical studies and needs explicit data-quality controls.
notes: Good support for dataset curation motivation.

paper_title: Large Language Models for Issue Report Classification
task: Issue report classification using LLMs
agent_or_llm_setup: Large language models for issue type prediction
key_findings: Evaluates LLMs in the NLBSE issue-classification setting and connects LLM prompting to established issue-label benchmarks.
relevance_to_autoempirical: Relevant as a compact benchmark-style baseline for AutoEmpirical filtering experiments.
notes: Candidate baseline paper; verify exact model list before citation.

paper_title: Issue Report Classification Using Pre-Trained Language Models
task: Automatic GitHub issue classification
agent_or_llm_setup: Fine-tuned BERT-based language models, best with RoBERTa
key_findings: Reports fine-tuned RoBERTa reaching strong issue classification performance on GitHub issues.
relevance_to_autoempirical: Useful supervised encoder baseline for comparing against single-agent and MAS prompting.
notes: NLBSE 2022/2023 lineage.

paper_title: Impact of data quality for automatic issue classification using pre-trained language models
task: Automatic issue classification and data-quality analysis
data_source: Public GitHub and Jira issue datasets
agent_or_llm_setup: Fine-tuned BERT and variants
key_findings: Finds RoBERTa-based classifiers strong, while generic data-quality filters did not consistently improve performance.
relevance_to_autoempirical: Relevant because AutoEmpirical merges multiple paper artifacts and should report how label/source quality affects model results.
notes: Use to motivate quality report and source heterogeneity.

paper_title: CatIss: An Intelligent Tool for Categorizing Issues Reports using Transformers
task: Classify issue reports into bug, enhancement, and question
agent_or_llm_setup: Fine-tuned RoBERTa classifier
key_findings: Reports 87.2 micro-F1 and generalization across repositories with little project history.
relevance_to_autoempirical: Relevant as a simple reproducible encoder baseline for AutoEmpirical issue filtering.
notes: Tool-style baseline; has public scripts.

paper_title: Predicting Issue Types on GitHub
task: Assign issue type labels on GitHub
agent_or_llm_setup: TicketTagger machine-learning classifier
key_findings: Introduces TicketTagger for bug/enhancement/question labeling from issue text.
relevance_to_autoempirical: Relevant as an older non-LLM issue-labeling baseline and as a baseline referenced by CatIss/NLBSE work.
notes: Use as traditional ML baseline.

paper_title: Text-to-text Generation for Issue Report Classification
task: Issue report classification as text-to-text generation
agent_or_llm_setup: Fine-tuned FLAN-T5-style text-to-text model
key_findings: Casts issue classification as sequence generation rather than fixed classifier output.
relevance_to_autoempirical: Relevant because AutoEmpirical prompts already require structured JSON labels and can compare text-to-text generation against classifier heads.
notes: Artifact-first source; pair with NLBSE proceedings if cited formally.

paper_title: A Multimodal Deep Learning Model Using Text, Image, and Code Data for Improving Issue Classification Tasks
task: Issue classification using text, image, and code modalities
data_source: Open-source project issue reports with attached artifacts
agent_or_llm_setup: Multimodal deep learning model
baseline_compared: TicketTagger and other issue classification approaches
key_findings: Shows additional modalities beyond issue text can improve issue classification in some settings.
relevance_to_autoempirical: Relevant because AutoEmpirical currently uses title/body/comments but could later add code snippets, stack traces, screenshots, or PR evidence.
notes: Useful for future evidence-agent expansion.

paper_title: Automatic techniques for issue report classification: A systematic mapping study
task: Map automatic issue report classification techniques
agent_or_llm_setup: Traditional ML, deep learning, transformers, few/zero-shot methods
key_findings: Maps common techniques, features, labels, and evaluation practices for issue report classification.
relevance_to_autoempirical: Relevant as the umbrella related-work source for positioning AutoEmpirical among issue classification studies.
notes: Use for related-work coverage and terminology.

paper_title: AI-assisted issue report classification
task: Reusable tool for issue report classification
data_source: Open-source, closed-source, and industrial project datasets
agent_or_llm_setup: Traditional ML, AutoML, and LLM-supported classification tool
key_findings: Packages several issue classification techniques and reports both benchmark and industrial validations.
relevance_to_autoempirical: Relevant as an engineering baseline/tooling reference for making AutoEmpirical results reusable.
notes: Software publication; useful for tooling comparison.

paper_title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
category: LLM / agent for software engineering bugs
task: Resolve real GitHub issues by editing code
data_source: 2,294 issue-PR task instances from 12 Python repositories
agent_or_llm_setup: Language models with retrieved code context and patch generation
baseline_compared: BM25 retrieval, oracle context, SWE-Llama, frontier LMs
metrics: Resolved issue rate via fail-to-pass tests
key_findings: Shows real issue resolution is much harder than isolated coding tasks and needs repository-scale reasoning.
relevance_to_autoempirical: Relevant because AutoEmpirical also treats GitHub issues as empirical units and can borrow issue/PR/test-grounded evaluation ideas.
notes: Core benchmark for LLM software engineering agents.

paper_title: SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering
category: LLM / agent for software engineering bugs
task: Autonomous software-engineering task solving
agent_or_llm_setup: LM agent with custom agent-computer interface for file editing, navigation, and tests
key_findings: Shows interface design materially improves software agents on repository tasks.
relevance_to_autoempirical: Relevant to AutoEmpirical because role agents may need evidence-retrieval and tool-use interfaces rather than prompt-only classification.
notes: Use for agent-tool-interface design.

paper_title: Agentless: Demystifying LLM-based Software Engineering Agents
category: LLM / agent for software engineering bugs
task: Simplify LLM-based software issue repair without complex autonomy
agent_or_llm_setup: Structured localization, repair, and patch selection with LLM calls
metrics: Issue resolution rate and ablation analyses
key_findings: Argues simpler structured workflows can match or exceed complex agents for some software repair tasks.
relevance_to_autoempirical: Relevant as a cautionary baseline: AutoEmpirical should compare MAS against simpler single-agent or staged prompting workflows.
notes: Important for avoiding overclaiming MAS benefit.

paper_title: AutoCodeRover: Autonomous Program Improvement
category: LLM / agent for software engineering bugs
task: Autonomously solve GitHub issues and improve programs
agent_or_llm_setup: LLM agent with code search, context retrieval, and patch generation
baseline_compared: Existing automated program repair and LLM baselines
key_findings: Uses autonomous exploration and patch generation to address issue-level program improvement.
relevance_to_autoempirical: Relevant because it operationalizes issue-to-fix workflows that are adjacent to AutoEmpirical issue analysis.
notes: Good agentic bug-fixing baseline.

paper_title: An Empirical Study on LLM-based Agents for Automated Bug Fixing
category: LLM / agent for software engineering bugs
task: Evaluate LLM agents and non-agent systems for automated bug fixing
agent_or_llm_setup: Seven proprietary and open-source bug-fixing systems plus RepoFixer analysis
metrics: Resolution rate, fault localization, bug reproduction
key_findings: Finds agentic flow, localization, and dynamic reproduction affect bug-fixing success.
relevance_to_autoempirical: Relevant because it is an empirical study of LLM agents on bug tasks and motivates evidence, critic, and reproduction-aware roles.
notes: Closest agent+bug empirical-study paper.

paper_title: ChatDev: Communicative Agents for Software Development
task: End-to-end software development through role-based agent communication
agent_or_llm_setup: Specialized LLM agents coordinated by chat chains and communicative dehallucination
baseline_compared: Single-agent and other multi-agent software frameworks
key_findings: Shows role-based multi-agent communication can coordinate design, coding, testing, and documentation.
relevance_to_autoempirical: Relevant because AutoEmpirical uses role agents and critic/arbitrator communication for empirical bug analysis.
notes: Map ChatDev roles to AutoEmpirical MAS roles.

paper_title: MetaGPT: Meta Programming for A Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework
task: Multi-agent collaborative software engineering
agent_or_llm_setup: SOP-driven agents with product manager, architect, engineer, QA roles
key_findings: Encodes standardized operating procedures into role prompts to reduce cascading hallucinations.
relevance_to_autoempirical: Relevant because AutoEmpirical can justify its evidence->classifier->critic->arbitrator workflow as an SOP-style MAS.
notes: Use for SOP and role specialization framing.

paper_title: Self-collaboration Code Generation via ChatGPT
venue_or_source: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology / arXiv
task: Collaborative code generation
agent_or_llm_setup: Analyst, coder, and tester LLM roles
key_findings: Reports sizeable Pass@1 improvements from role-based self-collaboration over a base LLM agent.
relevance_to_autoempirical: Relevant as evidence that role decomposition can help complex software tasks, supporting MAS variants in AutoEmpirical.
notes: Useful role-decomposition baseline.

paper_title: ResearchAgent: Iterative Research Idea Generation over Scientific Literature with Large Language Models
task: Generate research problems, methods, and experiment designs from literature
data_source: Scientific papers, academic graph, and concept knowledge store
agent_or_llm_setup: Research agent plus multiple reviewing agents with iterative feedback
key_findings: Uses retrieval over literature plus reviewer agents to iteratively refine research ideas.
relevance_to_autoempirical: Relevant to the broader auto-research framing of AutoEmpirical, especially reviewer/critic roles for research synthesis.
notes: Strong analogy for critic/reviewer agents.

paper_title: AutoSurvey: Large Language Models Can Automatically Write Surveys
task: Automatically generate literature surveys
agent_or_llm_setup: Retrieval, outline generation, subsection drafting, integration, evaluation
metrics: Citation quality, content quality, survey length settings
key_findings: Proposes a structured pipeline for retrieval, outlining, drafting, and evaluation of surveys.
relevance_to_autoempirical: Relevant because Yanjie's current task is related-work retrieval and organization for AutoEmpirical.
notes: Can inspire an automated related-work baseline.

paper_title: Assisting in Writing Wikipedia-like Articles From Scratch with Large Language Models
task: Generate grounded long-form articles from scratch
agent_or_llm_setup: STORM: multi-perspective question asking, retrieval, outline synthesis, article generation
key_findings: Improves organization and breadth by asking questions from multiple perspectives before writing.
relevance_to_autoempirical: Relevant because AutoEmpirical related works can use perspective-guided retrieval across bug studies, LLM issue labeling, MAS, and auto-research.
notes: Use for retrieval and outline design.

paper_title: The AI Scientist: Towards Fully Automated Open-Ended Scientific Discovery
task: Automate scientific discovery loops
agent_or_llm_setup: Idea generation, experiment execution, visualization, paper writing, simulated review
metrics: Automated reviewer scores, generated-paper quality, cost
key_findings: Demonstrates an end-to-end research agent with automated paper writing and simulated peer review.
relevance_to_autoempirical: Relevant as a broad auto-research upper bound, but less directly tied to empirical bug-study labeling than issue-classification work.
notes: Use only as broad auto-research context.
